title: Hof operation lock (v2, backup/restore only)
description: /var/lib/hof/state/lock.json for a backup or restore operation - exclusive ownership of an in-progress or interrupted one against this host. Scoped strictly to operationKind backup/restore, never apply: the existing apply executor (scripts/operation-journal.mjs, unchanged by this item) reads and writes operation-lock-v1 exclusively and always will, for every apply run, old or new - there is no migration of apply onto v2 in this item, and no ambiguity about which schema an apply lock validates against. The cross-kind exclusion ADR 0006 promises (a backup/restore in progress refuses a concurrent apply, and vice versa) is enforced by the separate, lower-level physical execution mutex the ADR's own Decision describes - a later PR's executor primitive, not this document shape; v1 and v2 lock.json are two independent per-kind-family documents layered on top of that one shared mutex, never merged into one schema. Otherwise identical to operation-lock-v1 except for the added operationKind field. A pre-existing lock.json written before this ADR has no operationKind field at all and does not validate against this schema - an executor reading it must treat that absence as an implicit "apply" (operation-lock-v1 is still valid, still readable, never deleted). Deliberately has no TTL/expiry field - the lock must survive the invoking process dying (an operator's laptop sleeping, a network drop), so it is only ever removed by a successful commit or reclaimed by --resume for the SAME operationId, never by simply waiting it out.

operationKind.description: Which of the two new operation state machines this lock belongs to - never apply (see this schema's own top-level description for why).

operationId.description: This operation's own unique identifier - ties the lock to its operation journal (same field name) and to every operation-event-v2 record it emits.

approvedPlanId.description: The approved plan's own planId - a plan-v2, backup-plan-v1, or restore-plan-v1 planId depending on operationKind (all three use the same sha256-of-inputs shape).

acquiredBy.description: Informational only, for a human debugging a stuck lock - never used for an actual security decision (the lock's own operationId is the only thing that authorizes a resume).

targetBinding.description: The exact target this operation was approved against - see plan-v2.schema.json's own `target` for the full description of each field. Duplicated here (not $ref'd across files - no schema in this repo cross-references another by $id) so this schema stays independently valid on its own.

hostKeySha256.description: The exact accepted SSH host-key fingerprint from the same connection the bound plan was computed against - null only in --target-mode local. A host-key change invalidates every plan bound to the old one.

allOf.description: ADR 0006 review: operation-lock-v1's own targetBinding left this pairing unenforced by schema (prose-only) - v2 (this schema) closes it. Not backported to operation-lock-v1 itself, which stays untouched.
